title: First teacher Manetta, her mother's late playing, and parties at nine
summary: Her father did not teach her; Manetta did, then lessons at St. Mary's Academy; her mother played piano until she died; she played parties with her violinist brother at nine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was your father playing music then that you can remember?
Oh, yes, yes, yes. I played with him.
Played with him. Who was your first teacher? Did he help you or did you go to someone else?
No, my father didn't help me. Professor Mineta taught me my first lessons. And then when I was in high school at St. Mary's Academy, I took some of the lessons from then.
Did your mother still play at that time?
Yes, she played until she died. She did all the time? She died New Year's Day. Yes, I remember.
That's right. She played piano the night before she died.
She did that late. I didn't know if she kept the...

That's right. Yes, you were at the funeral. I remember that. Well, that, the New Year's Eve night, there was a party at my sister's house and she played the piano. She played that late. She played insane.
That's remarkable. Yes. Did she ever help you much with the piano in your home? No doubt she was... Well, I didn't need help

because I was so interested and enthused all I needed for her was to buy a piano. That was all. And I went right to work on it. And when I was nine years old, my brother, he was a violinist. And I went out and played parties at nine years old with my brother. That's right. Nine years old. I was playing parties. And then when I was 13 is when I started out with Professor Mineta. I started playing in his band. Yes.
